rounds.learn: A for loop runs the same code once for each item in a list. Each time around, the name after for holds the next item.
rounds.task: Print every tool, one per line.
rounds.say: Three lines from two lines of code. That is the point of a loop.

rounds.learn: range(1, 4) gives the numbers from 1 up to 4, but not 4 itself. So you get 1, 2 and 3.

rounds.task: Add up the numbers 1 to 5 with a loop. Call each number n.
rounds.code:
total = 0
[[for n in range(1, 6):]]
    [[total = total + n]]
print([[total]])
rounds.say: 15. The loop added 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 into total.

rounds.task: Use a loop to print 2, 4 and 6, each on its own line.
rounds.hint: for n in range(1, 4): and under it print(n * 2).

checks.msg: I need 2, 4 and 6 on separate lines.
Use a for loop for this one.

rounds.say: 2, 4, 6. One line inside a loop did all of it.
